A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, central argument and recommendation benchmarks. Text, equations and figures are readable. v1 has no appendices; v2's Appendices A–E are available and included in the comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 1–3 report original reward, estimation-error and policy-parametrization experiments on MovieLens, Twitch and GoodReads.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original benchmark experiments, repeated-seed results and robustness analyses. Section 3 also adds a synthetic optimization-landscape example.

M1.justification: v2 introduces objective-aware support restriction as an explicit learning adaptation, including softmax policies restricted to the logging support and comparisons against unrestricted policies. It also changes RegKL's weighting function from exp(r/beta) - 1 to exp(r/beta). The existing PWLL framework and POTEC decomposition otherwise remain.

E1.justification: MovieLens, Twitch and GoodReads remain the real-data benchmarks. Coverage expands modestly through a three-action synthetic bandit in Section 3 and stochastic reward-noise/shift scenarios in Appendix E.4, without adding a new real-data domain.

E2.justification: Figures 10 and 14 add RegKL-LIN and explicit pessimistic comparators: PAC-Bayesian IPS, ES and LS, plus IPS with sample-variance penalization. POTEC is removed from the corresponding MSE comparison, and DM (Bayes) disappears with the old heavyweight/lightweight experiment. PC was already evaluated in v1's figures.

E3.justification: The original batch-size and learning-rate-schedule sweep remains. New experiments compare default Adam with tuned one-cycle optimization and introduce controlled sweeps over reward corruption, clipping thresholds, RegKL temperature, action-space size, cluster count, logging support and pessimism strength. These substantially expand evaluation design; Appendix E.1's newly disclosed defaults do not establish changes to the original runs.

E4.justification: v2 adds support-restriction comparisons, optimization-landscape visualization, MSE trajectories, reward-noise robustness, linear-versus-logarithmic objective controls, and sensitivity analyses for action count, clusters, logging support and pessimism. The heavyweight-versus-lightweight convergence ablation in v1 Figure 3 is removed, although both parametrizations remain documented.

E5.justification: v1 reports no seed counts or uncertainty bands. Appendix E.3 introduces five-seed mean reward and shaded standard deviations across three datasets and two optimizer configurations in Figures 7–8, substantially strengthening statistical reporting for the stability claim. This is newly reported repeated-run evidence, not an established increase in runs for retained figures.

E6.justification: New results show benefits from support restriction, lower seed variability for cLPI, and performance under noise, hyperparameter and pessimism sweeps. Figure 12 reports that POTEC can match cLPI on MovieLens with 1,000 clusters. The original batch-size/schedule results are retained, while heavyweight/lightweight results and POTEC's MSE entries are removed.

T1.justification: Appendices B–C supply oracle-policy derivations and proofs that v1 omitted or explicitly deferred, including optimization plateaus, local maxima and PWLL concavity. v2 formalizes the effective action space and adds stochastic-gradient convergence bounds under bounded-feature and bounded-weight assumptions, including variance-dependent noise floors, in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The optimization-over-estimation thesis remains, but v2 makes objective-aware parametrization a central contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. Its main prescription now combines preserving objective maximizers while reducing the effective action space with using PWLL objectives; v1 primarily advocated PWLL and lighter parametrizations.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability limits: PWLL cannot replace value estimators for evaluation or policy selection, end-to-end neural training loses concavity guarantees, and poor logging coverage can yield suboptimal policies. It also explains the expressiveness–optimization tradeoff of support restriction and the excessive conservatism induced by strong pessimistic regularization.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly documents sample counts, user-history splitting, SVD embeddings, trainable policy parameters, logging-policy construction, reward-model fitting and clustering. Defaults include logging support 100, temperature 1, 2,000 clusters and PC threshold 0.1. v2 also adds a code/artifact link. These are substantial disclosures absent from v1, without proving that retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: Section 3 explicitly relates PWLL to offline-RL weighted behavioral cloning, discussing AWAC, AWR, CRR and reward-weighted regression, and disclaims novel PWLL update rules. New Appendix A substantially expands research positioning across OPE, OPL, pessimism and online versus offline large-action methods.

P1.justification: The introduction gains an explicit contribution list, the estimator discussion is reorganized into standard and large-scale objectives, and optimization and empirical explanations are extensively rewritten. v2 adopts oracle-policy terminology, replaces the lightweight-policy subsection with objective-aware parametrization, and adds structured related-work, proof, implementation and experimental appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adds landscape surfaces, support-comparison panels, uncertainty bands, numerous ablation figures and a dataset-statistics table. v1 Figure 1 becomes v2 Figure 2, while the MSE chart is rescaled after removing POTEC and the old heavyweight/lightweight figure disappears. The document also changes conference template and introduces full-width appendix layouts.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly deferred proofs and provided little experimental-construction or uncertainty information. v2 substantially addresses these gaps through Appendices B–D, five-seed stability comparisons, controlled robustness analyses and implementation details. Clearer novelty positioning and applicability limits further improve precision. These gains materially strengthen the paper's support and reproducibility, outweighing the loss of the original heavyweight/lightweight comparison and POTEC MSE entries.
